cross.title: Revealing Dark Matter in the Dark-Electron Rate of Xenon Detectors
cross.summary: There is high interest in improving experimental sensitivity to sub-GeV dark matter (DM) that scatters with electrons, as compelling theoretical models seem within reach. At the lowest DM masses, most of the expected signal lies in the single-electron regime, but so do large backgrounds. Xenon experiments therefore either do not yet search there at all or, as in XENONnT, apply cuts so severe that only $\sim$$10^{-4}$ of the exposure is retained, with sensitivity set by the criterion $S \lesssim B$, where those are the signal and background counts. We advocate that xenon detectors instead utilize most of their dark-electron rate (i.e., the total raw electron hit rate) and perform an annual-modulation search, for which the sensitivity scales as $S \lesssim \sqrt{B}$. Modern DAQs already record this rate, continuously in triggerless systems such as the XENONnT and PandaX-4T DAQs, and within trigger windows in LZ, so no new hardware is required. Using measured dark-electron rates, we estimate the sensitivity of XENONnT, LZ, PandaX-4T, PandaX-xT, and XLZD. We find that dramatic gains in sensitivity are possible, motivating new analyses of present and future xenon data.

cross.title: Modeling extraordinary relativistic jets on the scale of the cosmic web
cross.summary: Recent observations of supermassive black hole jets extending up to the typical sizes of cosmic web filaments challenge our current understanding. In particular, the overall jet size of J152932.16+601534.4 ("Porphyrion") reaches $\sim 7$ Mpc at redshift 0.896. Magneto-hydrodynamic (MHD) models of relativistic jets have never been successfully applied to such extraordinary distances, requiring demanding jet-environment and flow stability conditions. By using state-of-the-art numerical simulations of 3D relativistic-MHD jets, we show that Porphyrion's observational properties can be successfully modelled in a realistic scenario, involving a jet kinetic power of $3.5 \times 10^{46}\,\mathrm{erg\,s^{-1}}$ and an external medium of a low-density galaxy group. We find that the pair of jets expands to $\sim 9$ Mpc in about $20$ Myr, implying that the jet grows with relativistic speeds for most of its evolution. Comparing this case with other jets of similar power propagating in substantially denser cosmic structures, we find much slower outflows that can only reach a few Mpc, consistent with the bulk of the observed population of giant radio galaxies. Our results make a testable prediction, i.e. future detections of even larger-scale jets in upcoming surveys and database searches will be invaluable in studying the demographics and feedback of the poorly known population of powerful jets, particularly in under-dense regions of the cosmic web.

cross.title: Constraining Planet Nine with Pulsar Timing: Orbit Determination Method from the Acceleration, Jerk, and Snap of the Solar System Barycenter
cross.summary: Planet Nine is hypothesized to exist in the outer solar system in order to explain the physical orbital clustering of several trans-Neptunian objects. A Planet Nine would systematically change the location of the solar system barycenter (SSB). Therefore, the precise timing properties of millisecond radio pulsars would measure the acceleration, jerk, and snap of the currently-perceived SSB under the gravitational influence of a Planet Nine. We present a method on how to use pulsar spin frequency derivatives and binary pulsar orbital period derivatives to constrain the Planet Nine parameter space. We find that searches for unidentified massive objects in the solar system require at least cubic and quartic variations in the pulse times of arrival (corresponding to jerk and snap, respectively) in order to uniquely constrain an orbit. Otherwise, additional assumptions are required to fully constrain the mass and orbital parameters of the object. We use our method to weigh the ice giants Uranus and Neptune and obtain results consistent with the literature. This method could be used to weigh a Planet Nine after a putative optical detection. Future work will use updated pulsar timing datasets that benefit from longer observational baselines and advances in statistical modeling and noise characterization.

cross.title: Time-variable tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems
cross.summary: Most stars in the field are part of binary, triple, or higher-order systems, which we primarily observe in hierarchical configurations that allow long-term stability. Over long timescales, hierarchical triple systems interact primarily through gravitational dynamics, but more complex interactions arise when stellar evolution drives mass transfer. In this paper, we study tertiary mass transfer in hierarchical triple systems using three-dimensional hydrodynamic simulations. We find that the finite separation of the inner binary produces oscillations in the Roche potential that critically alter both the donor star's variability and its mean mass-loss rate. For compact inner binaries, the mass-loss rate approaches that of a single accretor, while at larger separations the orbit-averaged mass-loss rate increases steeply, approximately as $\langle \dot{M}_d\rangle \propto \langle \dot{M}_{d,0}\rangle (1+C a_b^{6.1 \pm 0.9})$. For the $\gamma = 5/3$ polytropic donor considered here, this scaling is consistent with the nonlinear response of Roche-lobe overflow to the leading quadrupolar perturbation of the inner-binary potential, which scales as $\delta\Phi_2 \propto a_b^2$. We also examine the donor's response to periodic forcing from the inner binary and find a transition between individual and collaborative accretion that determines whether the transferred material can form and sustain a circumbinary disk. Our results show that the finite separation of the inner binary can strongly regulate both the rate and fate of tertiary mass transfer, constraining a poorly understood phase of hierarchical triple evolution.

cross.title: Gravitational waves in hierarchical triples with lensing and relativistic orbits
cross.summary: Binary black holes (BBH) may be formed near galactic nuclei. If such BBH systems exist, modulations to the gravitational waveform through time delays, lensing, and angular momentum precession could allow the presence of the third body to be measured in this system. In this letter, we advance the modeling for hierarchical triples by carefully including new relativistic lensing, aberration, and polarization terms. We show that the gravitational waves from this system can be computed exactly in the geometric optics limit by ray tracing the null geodesics and parallel transporting their polarization without a weak-field expansion. Our construction evolves the inner binary as if it were a post-Newtonian signal, and computes the environmental modulations efficiently with elliptic integrals. We find that this method improves the accuracy of such a triple waveform significantly compared to previous post-Newtonian approximations, and allows numerically efficient computation of the modulations. This lays the groundwork for future hierarchical triple waveform codebases, which can be used in LISA parameter estimation and detectability.

cross.title: Post-Newtonian expansion of the energy and angular momentum flux radiated to infinity: Eccentric-equatorial orbits about a Kerr black hole
cross.summary: We present analytical expressions for the energy and angular momentum fluxes radiated to infinity by a (nonspinning) point mass in an eccentric-equatorial orbit about a Kerr black hole. These results build upon our previous work involving point masses on eccentric orbits about a Schwarzschild black hole. We now adopt the Teukolsky formalism in first-order black hole perturbation theory to extend our methods to Kerr. We obtain the expressions using the method of Mano, Suzuki, and Takasugi, which provides infinite-series analytical solutions to the Teukolsky equation that we generate using Mathematica. The expressions presented are obtained as a double expansion in the post-Newtonian (PN) compactness parameter $1/p$, where $p$ is the dimensionless semi-latus rectum, and in the eccentricity $e$, up to 10PN and $e^{20}$, extending beyond prior 6PN and $e^{16}$ results available for generic orbits. We characterize how the PN flux coefficients depend on the black hole spin $a$ and $e$, and find a set of spin-dependent components that can be resummed as closed-form expressions in $e$. The analytical expressions are then validated with numerical comparisons against high-precision sample results from an independent Teukolsky code and with a broader set of numerically interpolated values derived from a flux data set produced with the same code. For $a=0.9M$, the numerically evaluated 10PN fluxes match current interpolated flux grids ($\sim10^{-7}$) for $p\gtrsim20$ to $75$ as $e$ ranges from $0.1$ to $0.7$, where they could replace Teukolsky-code results.

cross.title: Dissipative Tidal Love Numbers of Neutron Stars from Viscous Heating
cross.summary: We compute the leading low-frequency dissipative tidal response of nonrotating relativistic neutron stars. We formulate the response in a worldline effective field theory. We determine the linear dissipative Love number in two complementary ways: from the redshifted viscous entropy production inside the star and from the imaginary, frequency-odd part of the exterior metric. The first method reduces the calculation to an integral over the static equilibrium tide; the second provides an independent check. We apply our approach to publicly available equations of state and assess the corresponding correction to the gravitational-wave phase of neutron-star binaries. For an equal-mass $1.4+1.4M_\odot$ binary with both stars at a redshifted temperature $T_\infty=10^5\,\mathrm K$ and a standard electron shear viscosity, tidal dissipation shifts the gravitational-wave phase by less than $10^{-3}$ cycles between $20\,{\rm Hz}$ and $1\,{\rm kHz}$ for the four equations of state considered. Including the resulting rise in the stars' temperature in a simple thermal model reduces the shift below $10^{-6}$ cycles. For the viscosity model considered here, shear-viscous tidal dissipation in cold neutron stars is negligible for gravitational-wave phasing. This suggests that a measurable dissipative tidal signature would have to come from a different mechanism.

cross.title: Constraints on ultralight dark matter couplings from orbital perturbations of binary pulsars
cross.summary: Ultralight dark matter coupled directly to ordinary matter perturbs the orbits of binary pulsars, and the perturbation grows secularly when its frequency matches a harmonic of the orbital motion. We use this effect to constrain three couplings with the wideband timing data for the $50$ binary pulsars of the NANOGrav 15 yr data set: a linear and a quadratic universal coupling of a scalar field to matter, and a vector field coupled to baryon minus lepton number ($B-L$). For every system and for masses between $10^{-23}$ and $10^{-18}\,$eV, we build the timing signature from the perturbed orbital elements. We then sample the coupling together with the local amplitude, phase and direction of the field and the red noise of the pulsar, marginalizing analytically over the timing model, and combine the single-pulsar likelihoods into $95\%$ credible upper limits at each mass. For a universal linear coupling, the orbital resonances of the eccentric systems bring the limit close to the Cassini bound. For the quadratic coupling, treating the neutron star as a point particle, the limits are the strongest available between $2\times10^{-22}$ and $2\times10^{-21}\,$eV. In the case of vector ultralight dark matter, the limit is comparable to the PPTA and Eöt-Wash bounds between $3\times10^{-22}$ and $10^{-21}\,$eV and reaches or beats the Eöt-Wash bound at isolated orbital resonances, while MICROSCOPE remains stronger over the entire mass range.

cross.title: The Science Chapter of the Einstein Telescope Geometry Comparison Report
cross.summary: This is the Scientific Added Value Chapter of the Einstein Telescope (ET) Geometry Comparison Report, commissioned from the ET Organization by the ET Board of Governmental Representatives. We compare three configurations: a single-site 10-km triangle ($\Delta$) and two 15-km L-shaped detectors (2L) at widely separated sites, either nearly aligned or misaligned. We use metrics representative of the ET science case: compact-binary populations, dense matter, cosmography, stochastic backgrounds, multimessenger astronomy, fundamental physics, and continuous and burst sources. All three configurations deliver the ET science case, but they excel in different areas. For most sensitivity-driven science, the 2L configurations outperform the $\Delta$. The misaligned 2L is best for localizing and characterizing individual sources, multimessenger astronomy, and bright-siren cosmology. The nearly aligned 2L is best for stochastic backgrounds. The $\Delta$ localizes sources better than the aligned 2L and performs comparably to both 2L configurations for continuous and burst sources and at kilohertz frequencies. A 2L orientation of $30^\circ$ is a good compromise between stochastic-background sensitivity and localization. We validate Fisher information matrix (FIM) forecasts against Bayesian inference for $\sim550$ binary black hole and neutron star-black hole signals. Despite substantial differences, the FIM shows no systematic preference for either configuration for intrinsic parameters. For distance and sky localization, the FIM cannot capture multimodality and long-range correlations, leading to larger discrepancies, which however do not affect the ranking. Adding Cosmic Explorer to the network improves the reach of all three ET configurations, especially in volume localization and characterization of high-redshift sources. Differences between geometries shrink, but the ranking is largely unchanged.

cross.title: Relativistic dynamical friction and accretion for Kerr black holes
cross.summary: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs) observed by LISA will probe the environments of massive black holes (BHs), including the dark matter (DM) overdensities expected to form around them. We compute the relativistic dynamical friction and accretion experienced by a non-spinning compact object on circular equatorial orbits around a Kerr BH embedded in a collisionless DM distribution, extending previous results in Schwarzschild. The DM is modeled as a spike grown adiabatically from an initial Hernquist profile, and the momentum transfer is obtained by integrating relativistic scattering and capture cross sections over the full, generically anisotropic phase space seen by the secondary. Far from the primary the friction tracks the local DM density, which increases with spin. Near the innermost stable circular orbit of rapidly spinning BHs $(a\gtrsim 0.37)$, however, frame dragging forces bound DM particles to co-rotate, so that the secondary is overtaken by the surrounding medium: the friction weakens and eventually reverses sign where the DM density peaks. We show that a similar reversal can be mimicked around a non-rotating BH if the initial halo carries large net angular momentum, although this requires anisotropies beyond those found in cosmological simulations. We also show that commonly used Chandrasekhar-like prescriptions, which depend only on the local density, can overestimate the friction force. Our results demonstrate that the full phase-space structure of the environment must be included when modeling DM effects on EMRIs.

cross.title: Enhancing eccentricity through tidal resonance in binary neutron star systems
cross.summary: Orbital eccentricity of binary neutron star systems is a key parameter to reveal their formation history. Since binaries formed in isolation are expected to circularize long before merger, measurable eccentricity suggests dynamical formation in dense stellar environments. However, using numerical-relativity simulations, we show that eccentricity can be introduced in the late inspiral of an initially quasicircular binary, due to the $f$-mode resonance of one of the stars. We simulate the merger of two highly spinning neutron stars, one star spinning prograde and the other retrograde. Persistent tidal resonance with the $f$ mode of the retrograde-spinning star is observed, accompanied by a gradual change of its spin due to angular momentum transfer from the orbit. This spin change can be well explained by a simple resonance locking model that accounts for the spin-dependent shift of the $f$-mode frequency. These findings reveal an origin of eccentricity in binary neutron stars that is independent of their formation history and provide important information for modeling binary neutron star dynamics with rapidly spinning stars.

cross.title: Optimal Statistic for a Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background using Pulsar-Timing--Astrometry Cross Correlations
cross.summary: Astrometric measurements have emerged as a viable probe of gravitational waves (GWs), complementing pulsar timing searches by providing overlapping and higher GW frequency coverage. At its core, the search for GWs using astrometry is very similar to the search with pulsar timing data: GWs induce a change in pulse arrival times along the line of sight to a pulsar and a transverse angular deflection in the apparent position of a star. In analogy to pulsar timing, we develop a correlation statistic between pairs of stellar deflections for astrometry to search for a stochastic GW background. With a common formalism for both astrometry and pulsar timing, we also develop the cross-correlation statistic between stellar deflections and pulsar timing residuals. We estimate the signal-to-noise ratios from the correlation statistics and provide scaling laws in the weak- and intermediate-signal regimes.

repl.title: How Bright in Gravitational Waves are Millisecond Pulsars for the Galactic Center GeV Gamma-Ray Excess? A Systematic Study and Implications for Dark Matter
repl.summary: The existence of dark matter (DM) is supported by various macroscopic observations, but its microscopic nature remains elusive. The Galactic Center GeV gamma-ray excess (GCE) has been a leading candidate signal for particle DM annihilation. However, an unresolved population of millisecond pulsars (MSPs) in the bulge provides the alternative explanation for the excess. Identifying these MSPs in electromagnetic bands is difficult due to source confusion, pulse broadening, and extinction. Gravitational waves (GWs) provide a complementary probe: a steadily rotating, non-axisymmetric MSP emits a nearly monochromatic GW signal in the sensitive band of ground-based detectors, with amplitude set by its ellipticity. In this work, we systematically investigate the GW emission from the MSP population proposed to explain the GCE and its detectability with current and future detectors. We consider three major scenarios for the origin of ellipticity and model the population properties of these MSPs. We also consider both isolated MSPs and MSPs in binary systems, as well as Doppler effects in the detection. We find that while the signal is below the reach of current interferometers, next-generation detectors such as the Einstein Telescope (ET) and Cosmic Explorer (CE) may detect a fraction of those MSPs, offering a novel test of the MSP interpretation of the GCE. Future directed searches toward the Galactic Center may either uncover this long-sought MSP population or place stringent constraints on bulge MSP properties. Continued improvements in detector sensitivity will provide increasingly stringent tests of the MSP interpretation, with growing power to distinguish between the astrophysical and DM interpretations of the GCE.

repl.title: Pulsar Timing Array in the past decade
repl.summary: The past decade has been a transformative period for pulsar timing arrays (PTAs) and their search for nanohertz gravitational waves (GWs). This progress has been driven by collective advances in instrumentation for pulsar timing observations, increasingly sophisticated data-analysis techniques, and improved theoretical understanding of the origins of nanohertz GW signals. PTA sensitivity has steadily improved, leading first to progressively more stringent upper limits on the gravitational-wave background (GWB), and subsequently to the identification of a common red-noise process in pulsar timing data, the first hint of a GWB. In 2023, multiple PTA collaborations reported evidence for the Hellings-Downs correlation, widely regarded as the definitive signature of a GWB. These developments place PTAs on the threshold of a confident GW detection and the opening of a new low-frequency window on the GW Universe. In this article, we present an overview of PTA experiments, with particular emphasis on the rapid progress achieved during this pivotal period for PTA and nanohertz GW science.

repl.title: Modeling individual nearby radio galaxies as ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray accelerators
repl.summary: Nearby radio galaxies are among the most promising candidates for the acceleration of ultra-high-energy cosmic rays (UHECRs). In this work, we develop a physically motivated, source-resolved framework to quantify the contribution of the three nearest FR-I radio galaxies$-$Centaurus A, Virgo A, and Fornax A to the UHECR flux measured by the Pierre Auger Observatory. Acceleration spectra derived from detailed jet-acceleration models are combined with numerical simulations of extragalactic propagation, while the more distant radio-galaxy population is treated as a continuous background. By fitting exclusively the measured UHECR energy spectrum, we determine the relative contribution of each source and constrain the fraction of jet power converted into UHECR luminosity. We find that a small number of nearby radio galaxies can account for the highest-energy UHECR flux with acceleration efficiencies of order $10^{-3}-10^{-2}$, while the background contribution remains subdominant. The resulting scenarios yield mass-composition trends broadly consistent with observations and predict distinct levels of secondary neutrino fluxes. These results demonstrate that physically grounded, source-specific modeling of nearby radio galaxies provides a viable and predictive explanation for the origin of the highest-energy cosmic rays.

repl.title: An intertwined short and long $γ$-ray burst with a 4-minute separation
repl.summary: Gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), among the most energetic transients in the Universe, are traditionally classified into long-duration (lasting more than 2 seconds) and short-duration (lasting less than 2 seconds) events. Long-duration GRBs are typically associated with the core collapse of massive stars (type II), whereas short-duration GRBs originate from the merger of compact binary systems (type I). These different progenitor channels are reflected in distinct observational signatures that provide key diagnostics for GRB classification. Here we report a peculiar event, GRB 160425A, comprising two sub-bursts separated by 4 minutes: a short-duration burst ($G_1$) and a long-duration burst ($G_2$). Nearly all standard prompt-emission diagnostics, including pulse morphology, duration, hardness ratio, minimum variability timescale, spectral properties and established empirical correlations, consistently categorize $G_1$ as a short-like GRB (type I, merger origin) and $G_2$ as a long-like (type II, collapsar origin) GRB. The coexistence of merger and collapsar signatures within a single event challenges existing progenitor frameworks and calls for a re-evaluation of GRB classification schemes and progenitor scenarios.

repl.title: Visual Characteristics of a Rotating Black Hole in $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet Gravity with Thin Accretion Disk Under EHT Constraints
repl.summary: This study investigates the visual characteristics of a rotating black hole (BH) within the fabric of $4$D Einstein-Gauss-Bonnet gravity illuminated with two illumination models, such as a celestial light sphere and a thin accretion disk. To visualize the BH shadow images, we use a recent fisheye camera model and ray-tracing method. And then, we focus on investigating the impact of the coupling parameter $\alpha$ and the spin parameter $a$ on the shadow images. The results exhibit that the shadow radius decreases, while the shadow deviation increases with the aid of $\alpha$. However, with respect to $a$, the shadow radius is slightly increased compared to the corresponding shadow deviation. For a celestial light sphere, the increasing values of $\alpha$, lead to a decrease in the corresponding photon ring, while the space-dragging effect becomes more prominent with increasing $a$. For a thin accretion disk, we enhance its inner edge to the BH event horizon, and the particle motion is different in the regions inside and outside the innermost stable circular orbit. The result demonstrates that the shadow becomes progressively asymmetric with $a$, while the overall size of the inner shadow gradually decreases with the variations of $\alpha$. Subsequently, we also investigated the distinct features of red-shift configurations on the disk for both direct and lensed images. Additionally, we used the latest observational data from M87* and Sgr A* to impose certain parameter constraints on $\alpha$; the results depict the consistency of our considering the BH model.

repl.title: Advance warning of $γ$-ray blazar flares from Fermi-LAT light curves: a strictly causal machine-learning backtest
repl.summary: Long-term Fermi-LAT monitoring makes it possible to ask whether a blazar light curve shows signs of an upcoming flare before it becomes obvious in the $\gamma$-ray emission. We present a strictly causal machine-learning framework for forecasting $\gamma$-ray blazar flares from 3-d binned LAT light curves. Flare intervals are identified with Bayesian Blocks, and 42 variability features are measured from 365-d trailing windows. We train separate WATCH and TRIGGER models: WATCH predicts whether flare activity will appear within the next 90 d, while TRIGGER predicts whether a new flare onset will occur within the next 45 d. To avoid temporal leakage, all scaling, calibration, threshold selection, and validation use only pre-cutoff data (before MJD 60000). We apply the method to the FSRQ 4FGL J1048.4+7143, using 13 bright blazars as auxiliary training sources. Among logistic regression, polynomial logistic regression, and random forest classifiers, polynomial logistic regression gives the strongest held-out WATCH performance, with ROC AUC = 0.884, average precision = 0.392, and a block-permutation probability $p_{\rm perm}$ = 0.009. At the selected threshold it recovers 21 of the 21 positive WATCH windows. For TRIGGER, the same model gives AUC = 0.751, but with just nine positive test windows its AP = 0.121 is only about twice the random baseline (0.052), and no reliable pre-onset TRIGGER alert is obtained. The WATCH state appears before both held-out flares, with alerts 4.5 and 2.5 d before onset. These results suggest that the Fermi-LAT light curve of this source contains useful predictive information about its flare build-up during the period considered.

repl.title: Assessing the imprint of eccentricity in GW signatures using two independent waveform models
repl.summary: The gravitational-wave signal from merging compact binaries encodes information about their orbital and intrinsic properties. Over the last few years, state-of-the-art waveform models have begun to incorporate the effects of orbital eccentricity into their estimated signal. Over a similar period, many groups have applied these waveforms to characterize whether the imprint of eccentricity is present and, if so, measure this time-evolving property (at a suitably-defined reference point). In this work, we present a comprehensive analysis of 162 confident sources identified in the O3 and O4a observing runs of the International Gravitational Wave Network (LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA). Using the RIFT parameter inference engine, we employ two independently implemented waveform models (SEOBNRv5EHM and TEOBResumS-Dali) which account for orbital eccentricity and the effects of aligned compact object spins. Using these two waveforms, we find consistent conclusions that disfavor the eccentric hypothesis. Unlike previous work, among binary black hole candidates, we find potential evidence for eccentricity in three events: GW200129, GW231001, and GW231123. For the latter two events, the evidence for eccentricity is ambiguous, with different degrees of support from different waveforms. Consistent with previous work, we find conclusions obtained about GW200129 can be sensitive to analysis settings, as expected, given the nonstationary noise present.

repl.title: Temporal evolution of the periodic GeV signal from 4FGL J1913.2+0512 and analysis of the SS 433/W50 lobes
repl.summary: SS 433 is a microquasar whose relativistic jets precess every ~162 days, providing a laboratory for jet-interstellar medium interactions. We present a comprehensive analysis of 16 years of Fermi Large Area Telescope data (August 2008-September 2024) of the SS 433/W50 field, using events in the 0.3-300 GeV range and employing pulsar gating to mitigate contamination from the bright nearby pulsar PSR J1907+0602. We detect the GeV source 4FGL J1913.2+0512 (TS = 45, where TS denotes the likelihood-ratio Test Statistic) with a power-law spectrum (photon index 2.61 +- 0.08) and confirm a GeV excess at the western lobe (TS = 17). The eastern lobe of SS 433 is hinted at with lower significance. One additional GeV excess, Fermi J1909.6+0552 (TS = 20; TS = 28 over 0.1-300 GeV), located outside the SS 433/W50 system, is revealed after gating. Exposure-corrected Lomb-Scargle periodograms and precessional phase-folded light curves show a ~162-day modulation in 4FGL J1913.2+0512. The phase-folded emission is mainly confined to the first half of the precessional cycle, while the source is not significantly detected in the second half. This periodic signal is mainly concentrated in the 5-10 yr interval, remains visible in the cumulative 0-10 yr data set, and is not recovered in the subsequent 10-16 yr interval. Over the full 16-year data set, the modulation remains detectable but with reduced significance, consistent with dilution by the later non-modulated epoch. These results indicate that the efficiency and/or geometry of gamma-ray production in the SS 433 environment evolves on multi-year timescales.

repl.title: Measuring the Angular Auto-power Spectrum of Fast Radio Burst Dispersion Measures as a Cosmological Probe and Baryon Tracer
repl.summary: Fluctuations in the cosmic electron density are imprinted on the dispersion measures (DMs) of fast radio bursts (FRBs), making DMs a promising probe of cosmology and the spatial distribution of ionized baryons. In this work, we present the first measurement of the angular auto-power spectrum of FRB DMs, using 3455 apparently non-repeating bursts from the CHIME/FRB Catalog 2. We detect an angular correlation signal at $\sim 2.8 \sigma$ significance, associated with large-scale electron-density fluctuations. By fitting the measured spectrum to theoretical models, we constrain two key parameter combinations: $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$H_0$, which probes the cosmic baryon density and expansion rate, and $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$f_{\rm d}$, which traces the baryon fraction in cosmic large-scale structure (LSS). We further assess the sensitivity of the power-spectrum method to systematic uncertainties arising from the assumed FRB redshift distribution and from the DM contributions of host galaxies (${\rm DM}_{\rm host}$), the Galactic halo (${\rm DM}^{\rm MW}_{\rm halo}$), and the Milky Way interstellar medium (${\rm DM}^{\rm MW}_{\rm ISM}$), using mock samples. Our results demonstrate that the angular power spectrum is largely insensitive to uncorrelated DM components such as ${\rm DM}_{\rm host}$, thereby effectively mitigating the impact of poorly constrained host-galaxy systematics. In contrast to the mean ${\rm DM}_{\rm LSS}$-$z$ relation, this method does not require individual redshift measurements but relies only on the overall redshift distribution, and partially breaks the parameter degeneracies in the $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$H_0$ and $\Omega_{\rm b}h^2$-$f_{\rm d}$ planes. These findings establish the DM angular power spectrum as a reliable cosmological probe and a powerful baryon tracer.

repl.title: Uncovering Hierarchical Sub-Population of Binary Black Holes
repl.summary: The growing gravitational-wave census now contains 259 binary black hole systems with false-alarm rates below $1~{\rm yr}^{-1}$, enabling studies of trends, structure, and subpopulations that may reveal their formation mechanisms. We test whether hierarchical interpretations of previously proposed mass structure are consistent with the observed spins. We construct a multi-component mixture model in which each component has independently inferred merger-rate, mass, spin-magnitude, and spin-orientation distributions, while all components share a common redshift distribution. The model combines a power law with five Gaussian mass components whose ordered prior ranges reduce parameter degeneracies. We recover overall mass and redshift distributions consistent with published results, as well as the previously identified trend toward low, preferentially aligned spins at low masses and larger, isotropically oriented spins at high masses. However, unlike some previous analyses, we find that every Gaussian component except the lowest-mass component is consistent with isotropic spin orientations. Conditional on the adopted mass hierarchy, the inferred spins do not follow the mass--spin correlations expected from hierarchical mergers without additional spin evolution. Reconciling both distributions may therefore require additional physics. We present an illustrative, finely tuned spin-down model that could reconcile a hierarchical interpretation of much of the mass structure with the observed spin distribution.

repl.title: Dynamical formation of high-eccentricity compact binaries through BH--BH*/TZO collisions
repl.summary: The rapidly accumulating discoveries of binary stellar-mass black-hole (sBH) coalescences, detected by LIGO, have opened a new window into the formation and evolution of compact binaries. In particular, residual orbital eccentricity may provide a distinctive signature of their formation channels. Here, we investigate a scenario in which high-eccentricity compact binaries form through the sequential capture of multiple sBHs by massive main-sequence stars, using a combination of hydrodynamical and semianalytic few-body simulations. We find that sBHs with $M_\bullet\lesssim 0.2\,M_{\star}$ can be captured by massive stars and settle into a quasi-hydrostatic black-hole star (BH*) through gas dynamical friction. A subsequent encounter with a second sBH can then produce a compact binary embedded within the stellar envelope. Our hydrodynamical simulations show that through captures with small impact parameter, some binaries are born with high eccentricity ($e\gtrsim 0.5$), with its orbital frequency already entering the LISA band. Our semianalytic models further demonstrate that gas dynamical friction can pump the eccentricity to $e_{\rm 10\,Hz}>0.9$ before gravitational-wave emission eventually circularizes the binary during the final stage of coalescence. Once formed, the binary can merge quickly in $\sim 10$ hours. This channel may operate in dense stellar environments, such as star clusters and active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks. The same mechanism can also be applied to Thorne-Żytkow objects. A high-eccentricity binary in the LIGO band could therefore provide a distinctive signature of this formation scenario.

figures.caption: Illustrative summary of the scenario to form compact stellar-mass BBHs, which may happen in dense star clusters and AGN disks. The scenario initializes with the formation of a BH* in hydro-equilibrium, which requires a low-mass ( M ∙ ≲ 0.2 ​ M ⋆ M_{\bullet}\lesssim 0.2\,M_{\star} ) sBH colliding with the massive star at low velocity [ 75 , Paper I:] . A similar sequential sBH colliding with the BH* can lead to the BBH formation and coalescence.

repl.title: Formation of black hole stars via star--black hole collisions
repl.summary: In dense stellar environments such as globular clusters and active galactic nucleus (AGN) disks, stellar-mass black holes (sBHs) may frequently collide with massive stars. We investigate this process using semi-analytic models, three-dimensional hydrodynamical simulations, and one-dimensional stellar evolution calculations, focusing on collisions between sBHs and a $M_\star=100\,M_\odot$ main-sequence star with a radius $R_\star=16\,R_\odot$. We find that gas drag retains the BH within the stellar envelope unless the impact velocity exceeds $\sim2\sqrt{G(M_\star+M_\bullet)/R_\star}$. The post-collision outcome depends primarily on the BH-to-star mass ratio. For $M_\bullet\gtrsim30\,M_\odot$, the retained envelope is either quasi-spherical or disk-like, but remains dynamically unstable because of shock heating. In contrast, for $M_\bullet\lesssim10\,M_\odot$, the collision forms a ``black hole star'' (BH*): a quasi-hydrostatic, extended stellar envelope surrounding the embedded BH. These results agree with our analytic prediction that BH* formation necessarily requires $M_\bullet\lesssim0.2\,M_\star$. Follow-up \texttt{MESA} calculations further show that, for these low-mass BHs, the shock-heated remnant thermally relaxes without triggering runaway expansion. We discuss several astrophysical implications of BH*s, including their evolution, the possibility of gravitational-wave events from BH binaries assembled within a stellar envelope, and repeated star--sBH collisions as a pathway for rapid BH growth in dense stellar systems. This mechanism may contribute to the formation of massive BHs in high-redshift nuclear star clusters and may be relevant to the origin of the ``little red dots'' discovered by JWST.

repl.title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB~20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
repl.summary: We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}_\mathrm{host}$). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of $\sigma_\mathrm{RM}\simeq3.5$ rad m$^{-2}$. This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magnetoionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.

repl.title: Double Blandford: Resistive GRMHD simulations of accreting black holes simultaneously launch winds and jets
repl.summary: Magnetic fields can launch outflows through the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) or the Blandford-Payne (BP) mechanism in accreting black hole systems. Despite the dominant launching mechanism still being unclear, the BP process has been insufficiently studied in general-relativistic magnetohydrodynamic (GRMHD) simulations due to difficulties in generating and maintaining the required large-scale magnetic field geometry. Here, we set up six resistive GRMHD simulations of thin accretion disks with BHAC. The accretion disks in two simulations become magnetically arrested, while the others stay in the standard and normal evolution (SANE) regime. All simulations form jets and winds. The jets are parabolic and collimated by the outer sub-relativistic disk wind; a power law relating the jet width $x$ to the height $z$ as $x\propto z^\mathcal{K}$ yields exponents between 0.52 and 0.64. Among the SANE simulations, the setup with spin parameter $a_* = -0.9375$ has the most efficient jet. For a highly spinning black hole with $a_*=0.9375$, the BZ jet power is $\gtrsim3$ times greater than the disk wind power. The simulated wind regions consist of a highly magnetized region, where the magnetization parameter $\sigma\gg1$, and a less magnetized region. A fast outflow with the potential to reach Lorentz factors up to $\Gamma_\infty\approx25$ propagates in the former region, but because the Lorentz force acts against the disk, it cannot remove a measurable amount of mass from the disk. In the less-magnetized region, a centrifugally driven slower wind efficiently carries away disk material.

repl.title: Rapid Equation of State Inference from Multiprobe Datasets
repl.summary: Fully constraining the neutron star equation of state requires combining observations from various channels that probe different density regimes. We perform a joint multiprobe inference of the equation of state using gravitational-wave observations from binary neutron star mergers, NICER mass-radius measurements of X-ray pulsars, and radio timing mass measurements of massive pulsars. We constrain the parametrized equation of state and perform Bayesian model selection among a set of candidate equations of state. The joint analysis yields a radius of $R_{1.4} = 11.93^{+1.02}_{-0.83} \, \rm km$ for a canonical $1.4 \, M_\odot$ neutron star, and a maximum non-rotating neutron star mass of $M_{\rm max} = 2.31^{+0.23}_{-0.23} \, M_\odot$ with $90\%$ credible intervals. Gravitational-wave and NICER observations constrain the equation of state at low to intermediate densities, while massive pulsar observations constrain it at high densities by requiring the equation of state to support the observed neutron star masses. We find no simple correlation between the stiffness of an equation of state and Bayesian evidence across different observational probes.

Red error bars show twice the standard deviation of Bayes factors obtained using the bootstrap approach for GW and NICER posterior samples, with corresponding uncertainties propagated to joint analysis. No error bars are shown for the radio-only Bayes factors because the likelihood is calculated directly from the mass measurements rather than from a KDE reconstruction. Differences in the Bayes factors obtained from GW, NICER, and radio observations indicate the complementary sensitivity of the different observations to the EoS. See Tab. 4 for the Bayes factors.

repl.title: Local-equilibrium theory of neutrino oscillations
repl.summary: Miscidynamics describes coarse-grained neutrino transport under the assumption that flavor mixing is in local equilibrium. Here we introduce the concept of turbulent flavor-wave viscosity and develop techniques for including it in miscidynamics. This extension of the theory is necessary when neutrinos develop weak flavor instabilities as a result of astrophysical driving. The flavor-wave dispersion relation is obtained using a new and more general form of linear analysis, which does not require small flavor coherence. Flavor-wave transport is then approximated using wave kinetics and geometric optics. We hypothesize that the dynamical emergence of local oscillation invariants restricts the extent of flavor thermalization. In this view, flavor evolution is sculpted by both entropy-increasing and order-promoting factors.

repl.title: Effects of dark dipole radiation on eccentric supermassive black hole binary inspirals
repl.summary: The final-parsec problem has long posed a central challenge in understanding the merger of supermassive black hole binaries. In this paper, we investigate a scenario in which a dark scalar or vector field is sourced by eccentric binaries, leading to accelerated mergers through additional dipole radiation, and thereby extending the range of masses for which the binary can merge within a Hubble time. The Newtonian-order radiation fluxes from an eccentric charged Keplerian binary are derived using general results for localized periodic sources in flat spacetime. We find that dipole radiation, although insufficient to fully resolve the final-parsec problem, can alter the low-frequency spectrum of the stochastic gravitational wave background from supermassive black hole binary inspirals. We construct a simplified model for the spectrum and perform a Bayesian analysis using the current pulsar timing array data.

repl.title: A High-Precision Statistical Analysis of the SN1987A Neutrino Temporal Distribution
repl.summary: The interpretation of the SN1987A neutrino data remains limited by significant absolute timing uncertainties across independent detectors and a long-standing tension in the angular distributions. This work presents a high-precision statistical framework that resolves these issues by formalizing the mathematical distinction between intrinsic and relative timing offsets (ITOs and RTOs). By performing a simultaneous $\chi^2$-alignment of the Kamiokande-II and Baksan data with the IMB clock, we systematically incorporate non-Gaussian statistical correlations, reducing the temporal uncertainty by two orders of magnitude to the sub-second level. The $\chi^2$-analysis shows that Baksan's absolute timestamps require an advancement of $30.4\,\rm s$, while those of Kamiokande-II require a delay of about $6.4\,\rm s$. Establishing this unified, high-precision timeline is critical to test the physical nature of the first Kamiokande-II event (K1), specifically whether its distinct angular features signal the onset of the prompt neutronization burst. Previous literature often assumes that K1 originated from inverse beta decay (IBD) on qualitative grounds. By contrast, our multidimensional likelihood analysis incorporates energy, direction, and MSW flavor-conversion effects to provide the first quantitative constraint on its origin. We find a likelihood ratio of 3-6 in favor of an accretion-phase $\bar{\nu}_e$ origin over a neutronization-burst origin, thereby turning a traditional assumption into a statistically bounded physical inference. This framework provides the most stringent constraints to date on the chronology of SN1987A and establishes a precise methodology for future multimessenger observations of Galactic supernovae.

repl.title: Hybrid Stars with Post-Merger Rotation Profiles
repl.summary: We study the effect of differential rotation on hybrid stars with the first-order deconfinement phase transition from hadronic to color superconducting quark matter. The differential rotation is introduced within a realistic, four-parameter phenomenological rotation law, in which the maximum angular velocity of the rotating configuration is shifted away from the center. We focus on two classes of differentially rotating solutions, namely quasi-toroidal (type C) and quasi-spherical (type A), and study the changes in the star global properties and angular velocity profiles due to the presence of a phase transition. We show that when increasing the angular momentum $J$ the turning points of the $J=const$ sequences shift towards lower energy densities, shrinking considerably the region where differentially rotating neutron stars with phase transitions exists. Interestingly, for both type A and type C solutions, the angular velocity profile is continuous throughout the star despite the discontinuity in the energy density. Moreover, we show that for the differential rotation law we study, at the crossing points where the mass-radius curves for different equations of state intersect, the rotational profiles of the solutions are very close despite large differences in the energy density profiles. This reveals a possible degeneracy between the post-merger remnant properties for models with and without phase transitions, emphasizing the need for complementary multi-messenger observables to distinguish between them.

repl.title: Nonlinear Causality and Strong Hyperbolicity of Einstein-Israel-Stewart Theories of Transient Relativistic Fluid Dynamics
repl.summary: We present the first complete analysis of nonlinear causality and local well-posedness for a very general class of bulk and shear viscous theories of relativistic transient fluid dynamics, which encompasses (i) the original Israel-Stewart theory derived from entropy-current arguments, (ii) approaches derived from kinetic theory, and (iii) resummed gradient-expansion based formulations as particular subcases. Our work establishes, for the first time, simultaneously necessary and sufficient algebraic conditions for causality, alongside sufficient conditions guaranteeing strong hyperbolicity, in the full nonlinear regime. These results are rigorously proven for both systems coupled to Einstein's equations featuring a dynamic metric and on a fixed background, with or without a cosmological constant, and include baryon conservation (in the absence of heat/diffusion currents). The conditions are purely algebraic, require no simplifying spacetime symmetry assumptions or a specific equation of state, and allow all transport coefficients to depend on the dissipative currents. We also demonstrate that the normalization, orthogonality, symmetry, and tracelessness physical constraints on the dynamical variables are properly propagated during the lifetime of the solutions. Our results provide a readily usable toolset with which one can investigate the domain of applicability of relativistic viscous fluid dynamics in numerical and phenomenological studies in heavy-ion collisions and astrophysics.

repl.title: Exact 1D Nonlinear Solutions for Proton-Driven Plasma Wakefields
repl.summary: The analytical modeling of a plasma wakefield driven by a relativistic proton beam is an element in optimizing advanced plasma-based acceleration schemes. In this work, we present a 1D nonlinear fluid framework under the quasi-static approximation to describe the wake potential excited by a positively charged proton driver which attracts background electrons into a density compression rather than expelling them. We extend the classical 1D nonlinear relativistic plasma wakefield paradigm to evaluate the fluid profiles driven by intense relativistic proton trains under the comoving coordinate approximation. Using a two-bunch scheme, our piecewise-event integration model is validated to high numerical accuracy ($\sim 10^{-11}~\mathrm{GV/m}$) against independent phase-space quadrature of cold-fluid solutions, confirming that interface boundary corners represent physical step discontinuities in the second potential derivative. Scaling to an $N=100$ ramped micro-bunch train with fixed $2\pi$ spacing, we resolve macroscopic phase-accumulation and subsequent nonlinear detuning by deriving a piecewise analytical scaling model. This formulation maps the initial unattenuated quadratic coherent growth alongside the flat asymptotic post-train residual wake plateau, which is determined exactly by the conserved vacuum Hamiltonian invariant evaluated at the final bunch-train exit state. Furthermore, the framework estimates the onset of nonlinear phase-slippage that arrests growth and causes the transient wakefield overshoot to decay toward the residual horizon. Providing immediate 1D analytical benchmarks, this computationally inexpensive tool offers a reproducible baseline for verifying 1D fluid and multi-dimensional particle-in-cell (PIC) codes. It also provides a tractable starting point for exploring asymmetric, custom-shaped driver profiles relevant to transformer-ratio optimization.

repl.title: XRISM Reveals a Kinematically Coherent Core System of the Nearby Cool-Core Cluster Abell 2199
repl.summary: We present the results of a deep 251 ks XRISM/Resolve observation of the cool core of the galaxy cluster Abell 2199. From the integrated spectrum of the central $3' \times 3'$ Resolve field of view ($104 \times 104 \mathrm{~kpc}^2$), we find that the intracluster medium (ICM) redshift is consistent with that of the brightest cluster galaxy, within the optical-redshift uncertainty. This indicates that they form a kinematically coherent core system, which is offset from the mean cluster redshift by $\sim200~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$. The observed velocity dispersion of $\sim100~\mathrm{km~s^{-1}}$ corresponds to a three-dimensional Mach number of $M_{\mathrm{3D}}=0.16$ and a non-thermal pressure fraction of $P_{\mathrm{NT}}/P_{\mathrm{tot}}=1.4\pm0.2$%. Abell 2199 is one of the most dynamically quiescent relaxed clusters observed with XRISM, despite the presence of radio jets and a plume-like structure possibly associated with sloshing motions. Order-of-magnitude estimates suggest that turbulent dissipation could offset a non-negligible fraction of the radiative cooling losses, with $Q_{\mathrm{turb}}/Q_{\mathrm{cool}}\approx0.1$ for a large-scale driver such as sloshing and larger values for smaller AGN-feedback scales. Finally, we detect a localized enhancement of the Fe XXV He$\alpha$ $y$ line in the southeast region, which spatially coincides with a Chandra surface brightness discontinuity.

repl.title: A multi-band radio flux density catalog of ICRF3 sources using the Onsala Twin Telescopes
repl.summary: The VLBI Global Observing System (VGOS) is the next generation system for geodetic and astrometric very long baseline interferometry (VLBI). To optimize the observing time for each source in geodetic schedules, a flux density catalog is needed for the sources that are observed at the VGOS frequencies. The aim of this work is to monitor the flux densities of geodetic sources in the VGOS bands. The obtained flux density time series can be used for more effective scheduling of geodetic and astrometric VLBI experiments, as well as probing active galactic nuclei (AGN) physics. The Onsala Twin Telescopes have been used as a single baseline interferometer to measure flux densities of AGN that are part of the International Celestial Reference System (ICRF3). The telescopes observed at 3.2, 5.5, 6.6 and 10.4 GHz simultaneously. Both locally planned flux monitoring sessions and international geodetic experiments were analyzed. The data were calibrated using the Common Astronomy Software Applications (CASA). The possibility of predicting geodetic signal-to-noise ratios (S/N) using the measured flux densities was also tested. Simultaneous light curves in up to four frequencies have been obtained for 361 sources. The majority of the sources vary significantly in flux density during the measurement period. Most sources have a flat or inverted spectrum, with only 6 % having a steep spectrum. Furthermore, the flux densities from this work were shown to more precisely predict geodetic signal-to-noise ratios compared to the standard VGOS flux density catalog, especially for the most variable sources. Flux density variation needs to be taken into account to obtain the most optimal VGOS schedules. The flux density catalog presented here is expected to be of use for both astronomy and geodesy. We plan to continue the monitoring program.

repl.title: Testing PPN by the Rotation of S301 Star
repl.summary: The recently discovered S301 star, with an orbital period of 8.7 years and eccentricity $e = 0.982$, reaches a pericenter of just $140\, R_{\mathrm{s}}$--- approximately nine times closer than S2's $\sim 1200R_{\mathrm{s}}$ ---offering an unprecedented laboratory for testing gravity at large post-Newtonian counting parameters. We demonstrate that S301's stellar spin precession provides a novel probe of the PPN parameter $\gamma$, scaling as $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} + 1)/3$ relative to general relativity (GR). For maximum projected velocity shifts of $46.1~{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, next-generation spectrographs could constrain $\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}}$ to $\sim10\%$ precision; this forecast is conditional on the treatment of astrophysical systematics. When combined with S301's orbital precession --- a substantial $\sim 1.95^\circ$ pericenter advance per orbit (GR prediction), approximately an order of magnitude larger than S2's $\sim 0.2^\circ$, constraining $(2\gamma_{\mathrm{PPN}} - \beta_{\mathrm{PPN}}+2)/3$ --- the spin measurement breaks the $\beta$-$\gamma$ degeneracy. A projected MCMC analysis of S2 and S301 observations yields $\sigma_{2\gamma-\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ from the orbital precession and $\sigma_{\beta}\approx 3\times 10^{-2}$ (with $\gamma$ fixed to its GR value by the spin measurement; $\sigma_\beta\approx0.10$ if the spin uncertainty is propagated), with the $\gamma$ precision limited by the spin precession measurement to $\sigma_{\gamma}\approx 0.1$. While the spin precession provides an independent consistency check, its true significance lies in probing the same PPN parameters at unprecedentedly large counting parameters, where the non-linear and velocity-dependent PPN terms are comparatively enhanced.
